interpretation: Within gemma4:31b, confusion structure does NOT correlate with SigLIP class-centroid geometry (ρ ≈ 0.09, p ≈ 0.6-0.7). The MLLM's confusion is dominated by LM-level biases (teacher attractor) and prompt/text-image alignment, not by pairwise feature-space geometry. This is consistent with §5's prompt-variant finding that CLIP failures are semantic, not visual, and supports the paper's framing of the mechanism as 'class-neighborhood geometry' rather than 'class confusability'.
caveats: n=28 unordered pairs (8 classes) gives low power; only ρ ≥ ~0.5 would reach p<0.05.
gemma4 is an MLLM (encoder + LM head); the test conflates vision-encoder-side and LM-side effects.
A cleaner test would use a pure vision encoder (CLIP/SigLIP zero-shot, no LM) — not run here.
Image-set overlap with the 50/class centroid-matrix sample cannot be verified (filenames not persisted).
